title: Constraints and Concepts Introduction
learningObjectives: Identify template parameters and required operations.
Design a reusable generic utility or type.

understand.concept: C++20 concepts and requires constraints express compile-time requirements on template arguments. They can improve documentation and error messages, but do not replace understanding required operations.
understand.whyItMatters: Constraints state what a template accepts, making generic APIs clearer.
understand.explain: Read a concept as a set of compile-time requirements. A constrained call is accepted only when its argument types satisfy the requirements.

examples.title: Addable concept
examples.code: template<class T>concept Addable=requires(T a,T b){a+b;};\ntemplate<Addable T>T sum(T a,T b){return a+b;}
examples.explanation: Concept checks whether addition expression is valid.

examples.title: Integral constraint
examples.code: template<class T>requires std::integral<T>\nT inc(T n){return n+1;}
examples.explanation: Only integral types meet the constraint; include concepts.

examples.title: Printable concept
examples.code: template<class T>concept Printable=requires(std::ostream& os,const T& v){os<<v;};

examples.title: Floating-point constraint
examples.code: template<std::floating_point T>T half(T n){return n/2;}\n// half(3.0) meets constraint

examples.title: Size requirement
examples.code: template<class T>requires requires(T v){v.size();}\nauto length(const T& v){return v.size();}
examples.explanation: Constraint requires a size member expression.

practise.guidedTask: Analyze each Constraints and Concepts Introduction example: identify parameters, requirements, deduced or explicit arguments, and instantiated behavior.
practise.independentTask: Write a generic C++ utility or type demonstrating constraints and concepts introduction. Test two supported types, one boundary case, and one unsupported/constrained type; explain why it is or is not accepted.
hints: Begin with a concrete example before generalizing.
Name template parameters for their roles.

questions.explanation: Concepts check requirements at compile time.
The concept accepts integral type categories.
